instruction: Change the font of all slide titles to "Arial" in the presentation.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to last slide, selected title text, changed font from Calibri to Times New Roman via font name field, then saved. Completed in 11 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate slides, select text, change font name via Properties panel, save files
metadata.task_rationale: Extends single-slide font change to all slides, requiring iteration across 5 slides. Same interaction pattern but more steps.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing all 5 slide titles to Arial. Getter reads all title fonts from PPTX. Metric gives partial credit per slide (0.2 each).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads PPTX file, iterates all slides, and extracts title font names. Metric correctly compares each slide's title font against expected 'Arial' with partial credit per slide.
Expected parameter handling is correct: expected.type='rule' means metric receives {'expected_font': 'Arial'} directly, and metric accesses it via expected.get('expected_font', 'Arial').
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring state freshness.

Minor concern: Getter identifies title placeholders by shape.name == 'PlaceHolder 1', which is fragile. A more robust approach would use shape.placeholder_format.idx == 0 or check placeholder type. For standard PPTX files this typically works but could miss titles with non-standard placeholder names.

Minor concern: Getter only checks the first run of the first paragraph. If a title has multiple runs with mixed fonts (partial font change), only the first run's font is detected. Reasonable heuristic but not fully comprehensive.
Minor concern: If a slide has an empty title (no runs), it won't appear in the fonts dict but is counted in slide_count, which would unfairly penalize the score.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using shape.placeholder_format.idx == 0 or shape.placeholder_format.type to identify title placeholders more robustly instead of relying on shape.name == 'PlaceHolder 1'.
Consider checking all runs in the title text frame to ensure the entire title has the expected font, not just the first run.
Handle the edge case where a title placeholder exists but has no runs (empty title) to avoid unfair score penalization.
